conventions: ἐγγίζω and ἐγγύς head on the word that glosses the ἐγγυ- root, never on the supplied copula or the motion verb: ἤγγικεν → 'is at hand' heads on 'hand' at 21:8 and 21:20, ἐγγίζει → 'draweth nigh' heads on 'nigh' at 21:28, and the adverb ἐγγύς → 'nigh' heads on itself at 21:30 and 21:31. ἐγγίζω is denominal from ἐγγύς, so 'draweth' answers to no element of the lexeme and is the empty support word under rules 66 and 91, rule 104's φλογίζω → 'setteth on fire' being the model and rule 71's ἐγγύς → 'at hand' on 'hand' the confirmation. Heading ἐγγίζει on 'draweth', on the ground that 'draw nigh' reads as an ordinary verb phrase, remains the competing reading; 21:28 records a correction made in that direction.

An article the ASV renders by a supplied distributive determiner is aligned to that determiner and headed on it, exactly as rules 51 and 60 align one to a supplied indefinite or demonstrative and rule 89 to a supplied address word: the accusatives of time at 21:37, τὰς ἡμέρας → 'every day' and τὰς νύκτας → 'every night', give 'every' to the article and a bare 'day' and 'night' to the nouns. The test is rules 51 and 60's own — whether the determiner is the article's own to take — and no other source token competes for the slot here, no πᾶς standing in either phrase. Do not reach for rule 23 or for 'added' merely because the supplied word is quantificational rather than 'the'.

ὡς παγίς stands at the head of LUK.21.35 in the projection and the ASV translates it at the end of 21:34, so under rule 37 'as a snare' is added at 21:34 and both source tokens are unrepresented at 21:35, each verse's note naming the other. This is a versification difference and not a textual one: rule 97 is ruled out by name, LUK.21.34.v033 covering only s017–s020 and neither of its readings bearing on ὡς παγίς. The ASV's italicized 'so' at 21:35 is separately added under rule 5, the comparison it resumes being ὡς's and ὡς having already spent its English in the neighbouring verse. A reference comparison will report all of this as disagreement, and that report is not a correction.
report: Read all 38 verses end to end against the 49-lemma candidate table. No construction in this chapter is analysed two ways without the source or the ASV's own wording licensing the difference, so verdict is no-change and patches is empty.

Candidates cleared. ἐγγίζω: 21:8 and 21:20 head 'is at hand' on 'hand', 21:28 heads 'draweth nigh' on 'nigh' — one principle (head the ἐγγυ-glossing word, never the support verb or the copula) applied to two different ASV renderings, with the bare adverb ἐγγύς → 'nigh' at 21:30 and 21:31 agreeing. The 'for … sake' frame heads on 'sake' at 21:12 and on 'for' at 21:17: not a split, because rule 78 turns on the carrier's class and rule 95 classes ἕνεκεν improper against a proper διά — rule 78 names this very ἕνεκεν example.

πᾶς with 'things': 21:32 gives 'all things' whole to πάντα because the Greek is anarthrous, while 21:22 gives 'all' to πάντα and 'things' to the article τά under rules 22 and 102; the standing article is the licensed difference. 21:36 empties its article instead because ταῦτα has already written the antecedent, which is rule 32's apposition clause, not a third analysis.

Substantival articles are uniform: 21:23, 21:26, 21:35 and 21:36 split the pronoun or the supplied nominal from the relativizer under rule 32, while 21:21 keeps the discontinuous 'them that' whole because a prepositional phrase has no verb to carry a relativizer — the contrast rule 32 states in terms. Preverb particles are uniform under rule 106: the particle rides inside the verb at 21:1, 21:13, 21:14, 21:21, 21:28, 21:30, 21:32, 21:33 and 21:37 where no preposition answers to it, and the verb goes bare at 21:12, 21:34 and 21:35 where an expressed ἐπί takes the whole prepositional expression.

The 'added' units were checked by hand, the candidate table being blind to them. The chapter carries four ASV-italicized supplied words and folds three — 'shall be' at 21:7 onto the predicate τί under rule 63, 'he' at 21:8 onto εἰμι under rule 7, 'some' at 21:16 onto the partitive ἐξ — while marking 'so' at 21:35 added. That is licensing and not inconsistency: each folded word has a standing token whose English was still incomplete, whereas the comparison 'so' resumes is ὡς's and ὡς has already spent its English at 21:34. Rule 103's test reaches the same answer from the other side.

BSB disagreements: all five are articles this chapter leaves unrepresented under rules the contract mandates — 21:12 τάς and 21:34 αἱ displaced by a possessive (rule 20, the possessor unspent so rule 76 does not reach them), 21:23 τῷ displaced by the demonstrative τούτῳ (rule 38), 21:36 τά emptied by ταῦτα's antecedent (rule 32), and 21:15 οἱ displaced by 'your' where the ASV recast the participle as the noun 'adversaries'. None is a genuine error; each is the documented convention difference the report itself predicts, and no accepted edge was touched.

Three conventions recorded: the ἐγγίζω/ἐγγύς head, the article taking a supplied distributive determiner at 21:37, and the 21:34/21:35 versification split. No promotions or amendments: the article-to-'every' reading follows directly from the test rules 51 and 60 already state (whether the determiner is the article's own to take), and promoting it as a new rule on two occurrences in a single verse, with no corpus row for ὁ → 'every' in the precedent supplied, would be a weak rule paid for by every chapter after this one.
